import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_26/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_26/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_26/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_26_0 and Source3_26_1 on movie_id
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by title and compute average rating
grouped = joined.groupby("title", as_index=False)["rating"].mean()

# Rename columns to match target schema: ['title', '0']
grouped.rename(columns={"rating": "0"}, inplace=True)

# The target '0' column has float values that range roughly from -3 to 3.3,
# but the average rating is from 1 to 5. The target values appear to be normalized or centered.
# We need to transform the average rating to match the target distribution.
# Since no explicit normalization is given, we can center the ratings by subtracting the mean rating
# and then scale to roughly match the target range.

# Calculate mean rating from grouped data
mean_rating = grouped["0"].mean()

# Center the ratings by subtracting the mean
grouped["0"] = grouped["0"] - mean_rating

# Save the result to the target path
grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_26/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_26/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_26/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_26/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_26_0 and Source3_26_1 on movie_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_26_2 on user_id
join_all = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by title and aggregate average rating
result = join_all.groupby("title", as_index=False).agg({"rating": "mean"})

# Rename columns to match target schema
result.columns = ["title", "0"]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_26/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
